In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underlie the sensing and homeostatic responses of mammalian tissues to hypoxia.
the molecular mechanisms that control oxygen homeostasis in mammals.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of oxygen homeostatic responses in the context of health and disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

oxygen homeostasis is maintained by HIFs, which are activated in response to hypoxia and act as a master transcriptional regulator for the expression of a large number of genes involved in oxygen homeostatic mechanisms.
oxygen sensing is a complex phenomenon involving a multitude of oxygen-sensitive and oxygen-insensitive mechanisms.
oxygen sensing and homeostasis have been the most exciting and important discoveries of the last 20 years.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
oxygen sensing and homeostasis are mediated by the interplay between the gas-messenger, oxygen and the oxygen-sensitive transcription factors, HIFs.
we are trying to understand the mechanisms by which oxygen sensing and oxygen homeostasis are regulated in the context of normal and disease physiology.

oxygen sensing and homeostasis are regulated by multiple oxygen-sensitive signaling pathways, including the hypoxia-indicible factors (HIFS), the von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) tumor suppressor protein, the prolyl hydroxylases (PHDs), and the asparaginyl hydroxylase factor-inhibiting hypoxia-inductible factor (FIH).
The main takeaway from our work is that

oxygen sensing and homeostasis are highly complex and dynamic processes that require the coordinated actions of multiple signaling pathways, and that these processes are highly sensitive to environmental and physiological perturbations.
oxygen sensing and homeostasis are not only important for the regulation of oxygen levels, but also for the maintenance of other essential physiological processes.

oxygen homeostasis is achieved through the integration of multiple sensing mechanisms and the coordinated regulation of multiple signaling pathways, which together ensure that cells and tissues are able to adapt to the changing demands of their microenvironment.
